rule: Each 3x3 glyph on the left (read in pairs, top to bottom) stands for a stroke of a fixed colour, direction and length (U-shape=2 cells left, Y=2 down, 1-glyph=3 right, 3-glyph=4 left); the strokes are chained as a turtle path starting below the 5 marker in the right panel.
gap: Needs glyph-to-action binding (shape means direction+length) and sequential turtle-path drawing from a start marker; no module interprets glyphs as instructions.

rule: In each row (or column) the two same-colour cells at the edge define a step; the dotted progression is extended across the line, taking the colour of a third differently-coloured cell on the lattice and stopping there, else running to the grid edge.
gap: Rays are solid; needs dotted rays whose period is inferred from a cell pair per line, recoloured and stopped by an on-lattice terminal cell.

rule: The input shows a progression of shapes that grow step by step (with a cycling colour sequence); the output is the next, not-yet-drawn term of that progression (its size, shape and colour extrapolated).
gap: Needs sequence extrapolation over objects: infer growth step and colour cycle across a series, then generate the next larger term.

rule: All outputs are the same hidden 20x20 two-colour picture (up to D8 pose and colour swap); the input is a fragment of it, and the output is the whole picture in the pose and colours that place the fragment correctly.
gap: Needs a cross-demo object memory (one canonical image) plus registration of the input fragment against it under D8 pose and colour mapping.

rule: Each horizontal 777 becomes 868 with a vertical 6 bar through its centre into the 8-rows above and below; then the 3 end-markers of each 8-row segment are rewritten (kept/doubled or erased) depending on whether the nearest 6 to that end came from above or below (exact count rule unclear).
gap: Local stamp is learnable, but end-marker rewrite depends on a row-segment-level relation (origin of nearest 6); needs chaining a segment-level rule after the stamp.

rule: Vertical bars of different colours cross a horizontal 6 line symmetrically; the bar lengths are re-assigned in ascending order from left to right (each column keeps its colour, still centred on the line).
gap: Needs ranking/sorting of object lengths across objects and reassigning sorted sizes by position; no module compares or permutes object properties.

rule: The grid is a lattice of framed panels; in each row of panels exactly one panel differs from the others, and the output stacks these odd-one-out panels (one per panel row) into a single framed column.
gap: Has odd-one-out selection globally, but not applied per row-group of panels with the selected panels re-assembled into a stacked output.

rule: Each small chevron acts as an arrow: the cell a fixed distance (5) ahead along its pointing direction (orthogonal or diagonal) is marked 9 (or recoloured to 9 if a shape is there); where two arrows target the same cell it becomes 1.
gap: Rays use fixed directions; needs arrow direction read from chevron orientation, a fixed-distance landing point, and collision counting to choose colour.

rule: The grey staircase profile on the left is moved into the right box: each box column receives the matching left column's height of 5s from the bottom, and the coloured bar in that column is pushed upward (clipped at the box top); the left shape is erased.
gap: Needs cross-object column correspondence: read bar heights from one object and apply them as per-column fill/shift inside another object.

rule: Each blue plus-shaped 'emitter' with a short 2-colour seed beside it shoots a ray in the seed's direction to the grid edge, repeating the seed's colour sequence periodically (the example emitter already shows a full trail).
gap: Dynamics rays are single-colour; needs a ray whose cells repeat the seed's periodic colour sequence, direction taken from the seed side.

rule: Crop the region of solid 5x5 coloured blocks; inside each block, carve the 3x3 glyph of the same colour (found loose elsewhere in the grid) as background-coloured holes in the block's interior; glyphs with no matching block are dropped.
gap: Needs colour-keyed binding of a free glyph to a solid block, stamping its inverted shape into the block interior, plus cropping the block region.

rule: Single marker cells on the grid border define a colour palette; each long bar object emits parallel rays from its flat side (at fixed offsets along the bar) in those palette colours, running away from the bar until blocked or the edge.
gap: Dynamics can cast rays, but not choose ray colours from a border-marker palette nor emit multiple coloured rays at offsets along a bar.

rule: Each 8-shape with 9 'eye' cells and coloured tabs is lifted off, rotated/reflected so its tab colours face the matching coloured border walls, and placed so its 9 cells land on the loose 9 marker cells; original positions are erased.
gap: Needs docking: find D8 pose and translation per object so its 9 cells match the marker cells and tab colours face same-coloured borders.

rule: Several parallel anti-diagonal line segments of one colour are drawn; the background region lying between neighbouring segments (a V/triangle bounded by the segments and the opposite diagonal) is filled with colour 2 (exact boundary rule unclear).
gap: Enclosed-fill needs closed 4-connected boundaries; here regions are bounded by open diagonal segments, requiring diagonal-geometry region inference.

rule: A single multi-coloured snake path winds through the grid; trace it from its top end to its other end and output its cells' colours, one per row, as a 1-wide column (length = path length).
gap: Needs path tracing (ordered traversal of a connected curve from an endpoint) and serialising the visited colours into a new 1-D output.

rule: A branching path network links several patterned 'rooms' to a central hub; each branch of the path (from a room up to the hub junction) is recoloured with that room's main colour, while the hub stays unchanged.
gap: Needs graph/topology reasoning: split a path tree into branches at the junction and recolour each branch by the room it connects to.

rule: A small patterned key block (1s and 2s inside a frame) in a corner encodes a direction (incl. diagonals); every 4 dot inside the irregular outlines slides in that direction until it is next to the outline wall.
gap: Move-until-contact exists, but direction must be read from a key glyph that differs per task instance; needs glyph-to-direction binding.

rule: Each comb-like object has a notch on one side; a colour-2 block lying in line with the notch and of matching width slides into it, leaving a trail of 0s behind it; all other 2 blocks are erased.
gap: Move-until-contact lacks shape-fit matching (block width vs notch), a drawn trail of the vacated path, and deletion of unmatched pieces.

rule: Two same-colour L-shaped corner pieces mark opposite corners of a rectangle; a corner legend of 2-cell pairs (a b) says to fill the background inside the rectangle spanned by colour-a corners with colour b (b=0 means no fill), other objects kept on top.
gap: Has 2-cell legends, but the fill target is the rectangle spanned by a pair of corner objects; needs grouping objects into a region, with layering.

rule: Rows of coloured bars are separated by 7-rows with a 6 border column on the left; where a separator lies between two identical neighbouring bars, its left 6 is removed and a 6 is placed at the row's right end (plus extra 6 marks at open bar ends; details unclear).
gap: Needs comparing adjacent objects (are the bars above and below identical?) and moving a marker to the opposite end conditioned on that relation.

rule: A sparse dot pattern (dots on a stride-2 lattice) is a map: each dot becomes a copy of the template shape in the dot's colour, laid out at shape-size spacing and anchored so the original shape sits at its own dot; the dot map is erased.
gap: Fractal/tile is fixed; needs placing template copies driven by a separate stride-2 dot map with colours, scaled and anchored at the original shape.

rule: A small key glyph (colours arranged around an 8 centre) defines a colour substitution; patterns of the source colour are recoloured to the target colour and re-drawn mirrored/reflected about a line or point (e.g. lines on lattice positions), while key and unmatched marks vanish; rule only partly understood.
gap: Needs decoding an in-grid key glyph into a colour mapping plus a spatial reflection of the mapped patterns; beyond 2-cell legends.

rule: The corner cell's colour names one of the stacked arch-shaped pieces; that piece is deleted and every piece that loses support falls straight down (as rigid bodies resting on each other) until supported.
gap: Gravity exists, but needs cue-selected deletion and rigid multi-object stacking physics where non-convex pieces rest on each other.

rule: A small dotted key in the corner is a miniature layout; the part already drawn large (blocks matching one key row) fixes block size, spacing and anchor, and the remaining key cells are drawn as same-size blocks in that enlarged lattice.
gap: Upscale is uniform; needs inferring a scale, gap and anchor from a partially drawn enlarged copy and completing the key in that lattice.

rule: Each 3x3 framed box has a centre colour that points to the box whose frame has that colour; boxes at the start of such a pointer chain take the pointed box's centre colour, and the pointed-to boxes are erased (which boxes survive seems tied to the grey 5 path); rule partly uncertain.
gap: Needs colour-as-pointer reasoning between objects (centre colour refers to another box's frame colour) and chain resolution with deletion; association only matches same-shape templates.

rule: A 9x9 object made of 3x3 sub-blocks with an empty centre is 'exploded': its corner and edge sub-blocks are copied outward by one block step to form a 5x5-block ring pattern, and the hollow centre block is filled with a pattern assembled from the corner/edge colours.
gap: Needs part-level decomposition of an object into sub-blocks, displacing parts outward, and synthesising the missing centre from parts; no part-based object model.

rule: Each single marker cell is replaced by a fixed 4x4 glyph anchored at it as top-left, glyph shape and colour chosen by marker colour (2->4 hollow square, 3->1 ring, 5->6 diagonal blocks, 8->7 X); pre-existing glyphs without a marker are erased.
gap: Per-colour stamp table is close to behavior/pattern; needs asymmetric 4x4 stamp anchored top-left of a single cell, accumulated across demos, plus erasing unmarked glyphs.

rule: Scattered fragments (an open main outline plus small paired pieces) are assembled into one compact left-right symmetric picture: the main outline is cropped and the small pieces are slotted into its gaps/centre so the result is mirror-symmetric.
gap: Needs assembling pieces into a target object: choose positions for each fragment inside the cropped outline so the whole is symmetric; no assembly search.

rule: Four irregular shapes (one carrying a 2x2 colour key) are recoloured with the key's four colours by quadrant and fitted together, possibly rotated, like jigsaw pieces into a solid rectangle, which is the output.
gap: Needs jigsaw packing search (D8 poses plus placement so pieces tile a rectangle) and binding the 2x2 key's quadrant colours to pieces.
